_about: T632 (owner 2026-11-11): every piece the reach run could not place (any reason: straddles_the_cut, meets_the_line_at_the_cut, flows_to_the_sea_unjoined, leaves_bc_unjoined, ...) STOPS the run unless a row in `accepted` names it. Key: entry_id (a synopsis entry, or a DFO location id with kind "dfo"), rule_id ("" for an entry's scope or a DFO place), piece (section id), reason. An accepted row needs accepted_by + accepted_on; a row naming no piece of the run (stale) stops it too. `proposed` rows are NOT accepted: they are Claude's proposals for the owner, read by nothing; to accept one, move it to `accepted` and add accepted_by / accepted_on. A provincial piece that straddles a cut is never accepted (the straddle gate, T67: the atlas's braid sweep must cut it). Authored by the owner; read by pipeline.atlas.reach.build.load_unplaced_calls (reach run).

accepted.note: Noons Creek (gnis:23366), an added-stream piece of 2,199 m that reaches the sea without joining the creek's own line. The rule is 'No Fishing upstream of railway bridge'. Not checked whether the piece lies upstream of the bridge: if it does, accepting leaves closed water shown open; the alternative is a cut or an extent that places it. Owner 2026-11-11 from map A1: leave out. The piece is a separate added city stream line, at its closest 678 m west of Noons Creek's own line; not part of the Noons rule.

Seymour River (gnis:6105), an added-stream piece of 216 m that reaches the sea without joining the river's own line. The rule is 'No Fishing downstream of Seymour Lake'. Not checked whether it lies in that stretch. Owner 2026-11-11 from map A2: leave out. The piece is on the south shore of Burrard Inlet, 1,068 m from the Seymour's line; not Seymour River water.
